neighbours.label: 'first' in 'from the (very) first ...' (since the very beginning)
fire: She knew from the very first moment that they would be friends.
Right from the first page, the novel grabs your attention.
He has supported the team from the first season.
From the very first note, the crowd was on its feet.
We were impressed from the first day of the course.
The plan was doomed from the very first meeting.
Right from the first bite, the soup was delicious.
From the first chapter to the last, the story never slows.
quiet: She was the first person to arrive at the party.
The first page of the novel is missing.
He won the first game of the season.
The first note was slightly out of tune.
We met on the first day of the course.
The first meeting will take place on Monday.
The first bite of the soup was too hot.
Chapter one is the first of twelve chapters.

notes: Card: ' first' x4 after 'From (the very)', plus list nouns (valley, smiles) and ' of'/' and'. Probe: 'from the very first' 0.54, 'from first grade' 0.33, list noun 'hill' 0.49, 'faces!' 0.51. Mixed pole; tests the 'from the first' sub-pattern against other uses of 'first'.
